fields.question: Why does a Good verdict on a subset not count as a successful ScientistTwo research artifact?
fields.answer: The subset cheaply screens whether an idea merits escalation against a reproduced subset baseline. The full benchmark has an independent experiment and critic and can still fail or require engineering. The local gate preserves these outcomes rather than copying subset Good into full Good.
fields.example: Teaching example: a method is faster on short sequences but runs out of memory on the full long-sequence benchmark. It may qualify for full evaluation, but the subset result is not full-benchmark success.

fields.question: Why does ScientistTwo pass failed history to the Idea Evolver while also adding untried seeds?
fields.answer: Failure logs identify ineffective assumptions and engineering boundaries; dropping them invites repeated mistakes. Searching only around successful seeds also risks local optima. Each round therefore combines history-driven proposals with untried seeds ranked by external novelty scores. The local component does not replace semantic novelty judgment.
fields.example: Teaching example: early ideas all depend on slow retrieval, and failure logs identify I/O as the bottleneck. An evolved proposal may add caching while an entirely different retrieval-free seed is also tried, rather than merely retuning the old method.

fields.question: Can ScientistTwo's ablation and review loops replace ScientistOne's evidence-integrity audit?
fields.answer: No. The former schedules additional experiments, method changes, and writing; the latter checks score recomputation, rules, citations, and method/code consistency. A high external review score or a strict comparator returning true may still rest on fabricated logs or incorrect semantics. Passing control flow does not establish correct evidence.
fields.example: Teaching example: a rebuttal copies a score into a more polished table and receives a high review score. Independent execution and provenance checks remain unmet; another writing round does not make the score real.

fields.question: Why does the local stage return exhausted when the final Fig.4 critic requests refinement, rather than return the modified candidate?
fields.answer: Only the accept branch returns success in the paper's pseudocode. The last refinement is called, but no critic slot remains to accept it. Returning that artifact as successful would bypass the criterion. Separately, review_rebuttal does not generate an unreviewed revision when no follow-up review slot remains; both functions document their different accounting conventions.
fields.example: Teaching example: with one allowed critic call, old code is sent for repair and new code is produced. Since that code has not been evaluated, returning an object from refine does not establish that the bug is fixed.
